newsitem.title: USA: GM declines comment on bidding for Hughes.
newsitem.headline: GM declines comment on bidding for Hughes.

text.p: General Motors Corp Thursday declined to comment on a report that it has received a bid of $9 billion from Raytheon Co and a higher bid from Northrop Grumman Corp for Hughes Electronics Corp.'s defense operations.
GM spokeswoman Toni Simonetti said the report in Thursday's Wall Street Journal was speculation.
"GM and Hughes have no comment on the speculation," she said.

At the Detroit auto show on Wednesday, GM Chairman Jack Smith also declined to comment on the automaker's plans for its Hughes defense operations, saying only, "We're just going to have to let that play out."

GM previously disclosed it was exploring divestitures, acquisitions, alliances and other actions that could strengthen Hughes' defense operations, including missile systems, radar systems and other defense electronics products.
Many analysts have said they expect GM to keep Hughes' automotive-related electronics businesses and fold them back into Delphi Automotive Systems, GM's massive automotive components unit.
Hughes space and communications division, including the lucrative DirecTV satellite broadcasting service, could be spun off into a separate company, analysts have said.
